title: Live-step simulation of a deterministic instruction
statement: Let $m,d,k_D$ be nonnegative integers, let $\Lambda$ and $SD$ be state sets, and fix a Boolean input $x$, an augmented register machine $A$ with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, an initial label $l_0$, an oracle, a $k_D$-work-tape Turing machine $D$, initial decider states $q_0$, bounds $B,W,P$, labels $l,l'$, register assignments $v,v'$, a Boolean memory tape $M$ with head position $p$, and an output word $out$. Suppose the ordinary execution from $(l,v)$ with no prior answer takes one step to $(l',v')$ with no answer, the precondition holds at $(l,v)$, every register satisfies $|\mathrm{bits}(v(r)+1)|\le W$, and $|p|\le P$. Then for some finite time the compiled Turing machine, started with input $x$, registers $v$, memory tape $M$ at $p$, and output $out$, reaches exactly the corresponding configuration with label $l'$, registers $v'$, the same memory tape and head position, and the same output; throughout this run every configuration satisfies the bounds $W,B,P$ encoded by $\mathrm{MBox}$.
hypotheses_covered: A is an augmented register machine with m registers and d deciders
l₀ is the compiled machine's initial label
oracle maps each decider and Boolean word to a Boolean answer
D is a k_D-work-tape Boolean Turing machine
q₀ assigns an initial state to each decider
B, W, P are natural-number bounds
l and l' are program labels
v and v' assign natural-number values to each register
M is a Boolean-valued memory tape and p is its integer head position
out is the initial output word
the abstract execution from (l,v) takes one step to (l',v') with no answer
the precondition Pre holds at (l,v) with no answer
each register's v(r)+1 binary representation has length at most W
the absolute value of p is at most P
caveat: The auxiliary notions Pre and MBox are supplied only as Lean definitions; their detailed conjunctions are not expanded.
